title: Galois descent for a genuine semilinear matrix action
statement: Let K be any field, n a nonzero natural number, and b:G to GL_n(Ksep) locally constant for the Krull topology. Set T_g(M)=b(g) g(M) b(g) inverse. Assume T_1 is the identity on every matrix and T_g(T_h(M))=T_(gh)(M) for every g,h,M. Then there is a central simple K-algebra A and a Ksep-algebra splitting e:Ksep tensor_K A to Mat_n(Ksep) such that g(e(1 tensor a))=b(g) inverse e(1 tensor a) b(g) for every g,a. Conventions for central simple algebras and matrix splitting are those of [def-sc-brauer-scalar-defect]. No cocycle or realization of a prescribed scalar defect is asserted.

source.place: Lemma 03R6 (Galois forms of matrix algebras), preceding Theorem 03R7; explicit finite Galois descent expanded from the parent construction

proof.text: Construct T_g by the stated formula. It is a semilinear algebra automorphism. The hypotheses give an action. Construct A as its invariant K-subalgebra. Compactness and local constancy give finitely many b-values and an open normal subgroup N on whose cosets b is constant. Shrink N to fix all matrix entries of those values. Since T_1 is the identity, b(1) commutes with all matrices, hence is scalar; for g in N, b(g)=b(1), so T_g is entrywise g-action. Let L be the finite Galois fixed field of N. Then A is precisely the invariants of the resulting semilinear Gamma=Gal(L/K) action on Mat_n(L).

For v in Mat_n(L) and a in L, the sum over Gamma of g(a)T_g(v) is invariant, as multiplication by any h reindexes the sum by hg. If an L-linear functional kills every such invariant sum, linear independence of distinct automorphisms gives that it kills every T_g(v), in particular v. A proper invariant span would admit a nonzero annihilating functional, so invariants span. Select an invariant L-basis. The coefficients of an invariant linear combination are fixed by Gamma, hence lie in K. Thus this is also a K-basis of A and the multiplication map L tensor_K A to Mat_n(L) is an algebra equivalence.

The preceding basis proves finite dimensionality of A. A nonzero two-sided ideal extends injectively to a nonzero ideal of Mat_n(L), hence the whole algebra. Preservation of dimension under field extension implies the original ideal is A. A central element commutes after extension with the spanning invariant matrices and so is a scalar. Invariance fixes its scalar, putting that scalar in K; thus A is central simple. Nonzero n guarantees nontriviality.

Extend the multiplication splitting along L to Ksep to obtain e. The image of 1 tensor a is the original invariant matrix a. Rewrite T_g(a)=a by multiplying on the left and right by b(g) inverse and b(g), respectively, to get the required orientation of the descent equation.
